newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia holds French pilots for illegal landing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia holds French pilots for illegal landing.

text.p: Indonesian authorities on the island of Borneo have detained two French pilots for landing their planes without proper documents, the Kompas newspaper reported on Wednesday.

It quoted director-general of air transport Zainuddin Sikado as saying on Tuesday the two pilots, identified as only Sylvestre and Ricetto, had been detained since Monday at south Kalimantan's Banjarmasin.
An official at the French embassy in Jakarta confirmed the incident but described the problem as an "administrative error".
He said it was not clear under what conditions the men were being detained.
"It is being dealt with and it will be resolved soon," he said, adding the embassy was helping resolve the matter and expected the men would continue their journey to Australia.
Kompas said the pilots were flying French-made Thunderbird aircraft on their way from France to Australia.
It said the pilots had earlier landed in Supadio airport in the neighbouring West Kalimantan province to refuel, but managed to continue their journey despite lacking the necessary documents.
Kompas said the pilots did not possess any flight approval, security or immigration clearance documents.
Sikado was quoted as saying the French embassy had applied for flight approval on behalf of the pilots to the directorate of air transport in Jakarta.
"If the two aircraft are still grounded, it means they still do not have the other documents," he said. Kompas gave no other details.
